analysis:
Compared all supplied BASE/HEAD excerpts of provider-swift/Tests/ClusterSupervisionChecks/main.swift. The complete range map identifies only added tests at HEAD 248–330. Existing restart, liveness, link, file-permission, code-identity and login-agent checks are unchanged in the supplied matching source. New tests cover shared pairing update slots, staging before drain, mutual drain before install, partner failure/deferral, conflicting releases, disabled updates, stale/silent/unreachable partners, bounded waits, fail-safe unknown phases, one-time request consumption, stale-request deletion and progress serialization. No concrete security regression is established by these test additions; they do not themselves change serving authorization, encryption, prompt exposure, cache policy or billing. T-041's cache controls are not modified here.
Integration must examine the new ClusterPairUpdate implementation and cluster service callers referenced at HEAD 258–330: authentication/binding and freshness of partner progress, the actual fallback when coordination fails (302–303), preservation of release integrity and qualification checks (T-013/T-034/T-054), bounded drain/restart behavior (A-018/T-010/T-043), and request/progress file I/O safety under the local operator boundary TB-003. These tests use synthetic partner reports and temporary files; they do not establish those runtime contracts. Production implementations and callers are outside this supplied source scope, so their absence is a coverage limit, not a finding.
